title: Plugin hook exec form puts the script in args
summary: In a plugin's `hooks/hooks.json`, whether `args` is present is what decides exec form vs shell form. Exec form means `command` is the executable ONLY — putting `"node script.js"` in `command` alongside `args` fails to spawn. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` expands to the plugin's installed-version directory, which moves on every plugin update, so never write state under it.

body.problem: Your plugin's hook doesn't run, or runs with mangled arguments. Two causes dominate. First, exec form vs shell form is decided implicitly by whether you set `args`, not by any explicit field: with `args` present there is no shell at all, so `"command": "node scripts/format.js"` can never resolve (there is no executable literally named `node scripts/format.js`), and Claude Code logs a warning that the spawn will fail. Second, in shell form the expanded `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is re-tokenized by the shell, so an installation path containing a space silently breaks the hook unless you quoted the placeholder.
steps: Put the plugin's hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` at the plugin root, with the event map wrapped in a top-level `"hooks"` key. A file holding only the bare event map fails to load. An optional top-level `"description"` is allowed.

Prefer exec form for anything that references a path placeholder: `{"type": "command", "command": "node", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/format.js", "--fix"]}`. Each `args` element is passed as exactly one argument, with no shell and no quoting needed.
Keep `command` to the executable name or path alone in exec form. Move every other token into `args`.

To run a bundled script directly rather than through an interpreter, make it executable and set `"command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/format.sh", "args": []` — an empty `args` array still selects exec form.

Use shell form only when you need pipes, `&&`, redirects, or globs — and then double-quote every placeholder: `"command": "node \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/scripts/format.js --fix"`. `claude plugin validate` warns on an unquoted placeholder in a shell-form hooks-file command unless the hook sets `shell` to `"powershell"`.

Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` as "absolute path of the plugin's installed version". It is also exported to the hook process as the `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` env var (with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>`), so a script can read `process.env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` regardless of which form launched it.

Never write state, caches, or `node_modules` under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` — it changes on plugin update. Use `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` (`~/.claude/plugins/data/<id>/`), which is created on first reference and kept across updates.
Run `claude plugin validate ./my-plugin` before shipping; it is the authoritative check for paths, quoting warnings, and manifest shape.

pitfalls.whyFailed: Setting `args` switches to exec form, where `command` is resolved as a single executable with no shell tokenization. There is no executable named `node <path>`; Claude Code logs a warning because the spawn will fail. Split it: `"command": "node"`, and the script path as the first `args` element.

pitfalls.tried: Shell form with a bare `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check.py` after `python3`.
pitfalls.whyFailed: The shell re-tokenizes the expanded path, so an installation directory containing a space splits into two words and the script never runs. The docs give this its own error notification ("Hook needs quotes around a path with a space"). Quote the placeholder or switch to exec form with `args`.

pitfalls.tried: Exec form on Windows with `"command": "eslint"` or another `node_modules/.bin` entry.
pitfalls.whyFailed: "The `.cmd` and `.bat` shims that npm, npx, eslint, and other tools install in `node_modules/.bin` are not executables and can't be spawned without a shell." Invoke the underlying script with `node` directly, e.g. `"command": "node", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js"]`, or use shell form.

pitfalls.tried: Referencing `${user_config.MY_KEY}` from a shell-form plugin hook command.
pitfalls.whyFailed: A shell-form plugin hook whose `command` references `${user_config.*}` fails with an error instead of running, because the value would be re-parsed by a shell. Switch to exec form with `args`, or read `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_MY_KEY` from the environment. (Shell-form substitution did work before v2.1.207, so older examples mislead.)

pitfalls.tried: Caching installed dependencies or writing a state file under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.
pitfalls.whyFailed: That path is the installed-version directory and moves when the plugin updates, so the state disappears. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the documented persistent location.

pitfalls.tried: Matching the plugin's own MCP tools by server name in a hook `matcher`.
pitfalls.whyFailed: A plugin-provided MCP tool is named `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>`; "A matcher on the server name alone never fires." Write the full tool name.

pitfalls.tried: Setting `"shell": "powershell"` on a hook that also has `args`.
pitfalls.whyFailed: The `shell` field is "Ignored when `args` is set" — exec form spawns no shell at all.

body.verification: Build a minimal plugin with `hooks/hooks.json` containing a `PostToolUse` hook on `Write|Edit` in exec form, pointing at a bundled script that appends its received `$@` and `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` to a log file. Run `claude plugin validate ./my-plugin` (expect `Validation passed`), load the plugin with `--plugin-dir`, ask Claude to edit a file, then read the log: the arguments should appear exactly as written in `args` and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` should be the absolute installed-version path. To reproduce the failure mode, install the plugin under a directory whose name contains a space and switch the hook to shell form with the placeholder unquoted.
body.appliesWhen: Plugin hooks declared in `hooks/hooks.json` at the plugin root, or inline/by path under the `hooks` key of `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (both load and are merged). Verified against Claude Code docs for v2.1.302 (changelog dated 2026-10-16). The `onFailure` command-hook field requires v2.1.295 or later.
body.notAppliesWhen: Monitor commands and MCP `headersHelper`, which reject `${user_config.*}` and (for monitors) receive no `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` values and no exported path variables. Commands Claude runs through the Bash tool, in the main session or a subagent, never receive `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in their environment. Exec form on Windows does not apply to `.cmd`/`.bat` shims. Shell-form `${user_config.*}` substitution only worked before v2.1.207.
